data.name: Ribosome biogenesis

identifiers_status.reason: Gene and protein identifiers do not apply to the type "Biological process".

data.description: Making new ribosomes: rRNA transcription by RNA polymerase I, 5S and tRNA transcription by RNA polymerase III, and the translation of ribosomal-protein mRNAs. Distinct from how efficiently existing ribosomes work. Added 2026-10-10 after an audit found the Atlas had no node for it, although the 5'TOP mRNA entity already asserted that this output is canonical for mTORC1. Both polymerase branches gained a primary study on 2026-11-07: Pol I through TIF-IA (MAY2004) and Pol III through Maf1 (SHO2010). In neither case did the paper detect mTOR phosphorylating the target itself, so the branches are evidenced while the kinase step into them is not.
data.description_beginner: Building new ribosomes, the machines that make proteins. This is different from making the ribosomes a cell already has work faster. A growing cell has to do both, and mTORC1 has a say in each.

reading_levels.student: Making new ribosomes: rRNA by Pol I, 5S and tRNA by Pol III, plus the ribosomal-protein mRNAs.
reading_levels.research: Distinct from translational efficiency. Both polymerase steps now have a primary study in the corpus (7. 11. 2026): mTOR controls Pol I through TIF-IA (MAY2004) and Pol III through Maf1 (SHO2010). Neither is a direct phosphorylation - both papers looked for mTOR acting on the target itself and did not find it - so the output and its two branches are evidenced, the kinase step into them is not.

studies.title: mTOR-dependent activation of the transcription factor TIF-IA links rRNA synthesis to nutrient availability
studies.authors: Mayer C; Zhao J; Yuan X; Grummt I

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Mouse FM3A nuclear extracts and NIH3T3 reporter assays; human HeLa and HEK293T cells; rapamycin; in vitro transcription, 2D phosphopeptide mapping, immunofluorescence
studies.finding: Places mTOR on the RNA polymerase I branch of ribosome building. In HeLa cells, rapamycin (20 or 80 nM for 60 min) almost abolished synthesis of the 45S pre-rRNA precursor while the amounts of Pol I, UBF, TIF-IA and TIF-IB stayed the same, so mTOR acts on the activity of the transcription factor TIF-IA, not on how much machinery the cell has. Rapamycin lowered phosphorylation of TIF-IA at Ser44 and raised it at Ser199, two sites with opposite effects, weakened the TIF-IA interaction with Pol I, and after 2 h shifted TIF-IA out of the nucleus (nuclear TIF-IA roughly halved). Boundary: the authors write that mTOR activates TIF-IA either directly or indirectly, and report as data not shown that immunoprecipitated mTOR and S6K1 did NOT phosphorylate TIF-IA in vitro; Cdk2/cyclin E phosphorylates Ser44, the Ser199 kinase was not identified, and PP2A is proposed as the phosphatase that rapamycin unleashes. The nutrient link rests on a single experiment: nuclear extract from amino-acid-starved cells lost the Ser44 signal in the same way as extract from rapamycin-treated cells. Cell lines only; no animal or human data, and mTORC1 versus mTORC2 was not separated (the complexes were not yet defined in 2004).

studies.title: Requirement of the mTOR kinase for the regulation of Maf1 phosphorylation and control of RNA polymerase III-dependent transcription in cancer cells
studies.authors: Shor B; Wu J; Shakey Q; Toral-Barza L; Shi C; Follettie M; Yu K

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Human cancer lines MG63 (osteosarcoma) and MDA-MB-361 (breast) plus HEK293; U87MG, HCT116, HT29 in supplementary data; mTOR active-site inhibitor WYE-125132 and the rapalog CCI-779; SILAC phosphoproteomics, siRNA, ChIP
studies.finding: The RNA polymerase III half of the same output. Three hours of the mTOR active-site inhibitor WYE-125132 (0.5 uM) cut pre-tRNA-Leu by 53 to 80 percent depending on the line and also lowered pre-tRNA-Tyr. Phosphoproteomics identified Ser75 of Maf1, the repressor of Pol III, as almost completely dephosphorylated after mTOR inhibition. Dephosphorylated Maf1 accumulated in the nucleus and occupied Pol III genes more, while Pol III and Brf1 binding fell. Depleting Maf1 raised basal pre-tRNA and made tRNA synthesis insensitive to mTOR inhibitors, and Maf1 mutants that cannot be phosphorylated blunted the roughly threefold rise in pre-tRNA when amino acids were added back to starved cells. siRNA against mTOR and raptor lowered pre-tRNAs while rictor siRNA had little effect, which points at mTORC1. Boundary: direct phosphorylation of Maf1 by mTOR was NOT detected (reported as data not shown, and the authors themselves caution against reading that negative result too firmly; a rapamycin-resistant S6K1 partly protected Maf1, so S6K1 or another kinase may sit in between). CCI-779 gave a weaker effect than WYE-125132. The 5S rRNA result comes from the Maf1 mutants in supplementary data, not from drug treatment. Cancer cell lines and acute pharmacology; no animal or human data.

studies.title: TORC1 and PKA activity towards ribosome biogenesis oscillates in synchrony with the budding yeast cell cycle
studies.authors: Guerra P; Vuillemenot LPE; van Oppen YB; Been M; Milias-Argeitis A

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Budding yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae), time-lapse single-cell microscopy
studies.finding: Tracking the localisation of two TORC1 and PKA targets by time-lapse microscopy in hundreds of yeast cells shows that TORC1/PKA activity towards ribosome biogenesis rises and falls in step with the cell cycle even when outside conditions stay constant; mutations in upstream regulators suggest internal metabolic signals partly drive the oscillation.

studies.title: mTOR inactivation governs adaptive survival to ribosome biogenesis deficiency
studies.authors: Fan W; Liu H; Yang L; Sinha N; Catipovic M; Dong D; Easawaran H; Green R; Laiho M

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Human cancer cell lines (functional genomics/CRISPR screens)
studies.finding: mTORC1 inhibition does not restore ribosome biogenesis but redistributes limited ribosomes away from highly-translated 5'TOP mRNAs toward survival-essential transcripts, defining a 'translational fitness' mechanism that lets cancer cells survive ribosome biogenesis deficiency.

studies.title: The translational landscape of mTOR signalling steers cancer initiation and metastasis
studies.authors: Hsieh AC; Liu Yi; Edlind MP; Ingolia NT; Janes MR; Sher A; Shi EY; Stumpf CR; Christensen C; Bonham MJ; Wang S; Ren P; Martin M; Jessen K; Feldman ME; Weissman JS; Shokat KM; Rommel C; Ruggero D

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Showed WHY mTOR-driven translation matters for cancer: in prostate cancer, oncogenic mTOR selectively translates a specific set of pro-invasion mRNAs that drive metastasis. An ATP-competitive mTOR inhibitor (INK128) reversed that signature - an early preclinical rationale from mouse models and cell lines, not a clinical result.

relations.mechanism: mTORC1 drives ribosome production through both nuclear polymerases, and the corpus now carries one primary study for each branch. RNA polymerase I: rapamycin inactivates the Pol I transcription factor TIF-IA within an hour and nearly abolishes 45S pre-rRNA synthesis, with no change in the amount of Pol I, UBF, TIF-IA or TIF-IB, so the control is over activity rather than abundance (MAY2004). RNA polymerase III: mTOR inhibition dephosphorylates the Pol III repressor Maf1 at Ser75, Maf1 then accumulates in the nucleus and occupies Pol III genes while Pol III and Brf1 binding falls, and pre-tRNA levels drop by 53 to 80 percent; raptor siRNA reproduces it and rictor siRNA barely does, which places the step on mTORC1 (SHO2010). Around these two steps, TORC1 activity towards ribosome biogenesis oscillates with the cell cycle in budding yeast (GUE2022) and the mammalian translational programme mTORC1 controls is dominated by the ribosome's own components (HSI2012). The dependency also runs the other way: when ribosome biogenesis fails, mTOR inactivation is what lets cells survive it (FAN2026).
relations.mechanism_beginner: A growing cell needs more ribosomes, not just busier ones, and mTORC1 has a say in how many get built. The parts of a ribosome are copied out by two different machines in the nucleus, and mTORC1 reaches both: it keeps a switch called TIF-IA on, so one machine copies the large RNA core, and it keeps a brake called Maf1 off, so the other copies the small RNAs and transfer RNAs. Add a drug that blocks mTOR and both lines slow down within an hour or two. In neither case has anyone caught mTOR touching the switch or the brake itself, so something unidentified sits in between. The link also runs backwards: block ribosome building and the cell turns mTOR down to cope. Some of this was followed in budding yeast, the rest in human and mouse cells grown in a dish, not in whole animals and not in people.
relations.boundary: Both polymerase branches are in the corpus as of 7 November 2026, and both are indirect: neither paper could show mTOR phosphorylating its target. MAY2004 writes that mTOR activates TIF-IA directly or indirectly and reports that immunoprecipitated mTOR and S6K1 did not phosphorylate TIF-IA in vitro; Cdk2/cyclin E phosphorylates the activating Ser44, the Ser199 kinase was not identified, and PP2A is proposed as the phosphatase. SHO2010 likewise did not detect direct phosphorylation of Maf1 and points at S6K1 or another kinase in between. Scope: cultured cells only on both branches (mouse and human lines in MAY2004; human cancer lines plus HEK293 in SHO2010), acute drug treatment over hours, and no animal or human data on either. MAY2004 predates the mTORC1/mTORC2 distinction, so its complex assignment rests on rapamycin sensitivity alone, while SHO2010 separates the complexes with raptor and rictor siRNA. The 5S rRNA part of the Pol III claim comes from Maf1 phospho-mutants in supplementary data, not from drug treatment. The ribosomal-protein mRNA arm of this output is covered by the separate 5'TOP mRNA edges, not here.
